idea_name: Multi-Day Range Breakout, Flip Exit (NQ 15min, no stop/target — winners run to session close)
rationale: Iteration 3 (overnight_gap_fade) is retired as structural — backing the hardcoded 10.2 bps round-trip toll out of its realized net per-trade return leaves gross ≈ -0.7 bps, so its no-edge verdict stands. This variation retires stop_atr_mult/target_r, replacing them with a plain flip-exit on the opposite range break (winners run to session close, losers truncated by the flip instead of a stop priced at Close on an intrabar High/Low breach). Freed param slots buy range_days to raise breakout significance. Expected gross ≈ +16bps vs the 10.2bps toll.

idea_name: Rolling Range Breakout + Volatility-Regime Gate (NQ 15min, zero-param ATR-ratio filter)
rationale: Iteration 5 is rejected as overfit-gap, not no-edge -- it is the first entry in the log with positive OOS (CAGR +2.4%, PF 1.12, efficiency 0.4845), so the family is addressable and the lever is trade quality, not power (285 OOS trades, "only the trade-count condition passes"). Reading results/iter-005-rolling-range-breakout-flip-exit/fold_table.csv directly, the train Sharpe of the selected combo is 3.4-6.7 through the 2022 high-volatility bear folds (1-9) but goes negative in contiguous multi-week runs -- folds 25-27 (Aug-Oct 2023), 34-36 (Feb-Apr 2024) and 58-62 (Jul-Oct 2025), all calm grind regimes -- so the breakout edge is regime-conditional and the optimizer keeps re-fitting a channel that has no edge to give in those stretches. This is variation type (b), a zero-param added filter: volatility.md states plainly that in a Low-Volatility Regime trend-following struggles while momentum often works better in higher volatility with more pronounced trends, and that volatility clusters, so a slow realized-vol ratio is a persistent, multi-day regime switch rather than a bar-by-bar one. Both grids are kept byte-identical to iteration 5 so the filter is the only change and the result is attributable; the 192/0.15 grid-boundary pinning (37/65 and 33/65 folds) remains available as a separate, still-unused lever for a later iteration. Entry rule adds a hardcoded (non-grid-searched) volatility regime gate: ATR_fast (96-bar TR mean) >= ATR_slow (384-bar TR mean) required for both long and short entries, else NaN'd out. Exit rule unchanged: plain flip-exit on the filtered entries series, no stop/target.
